questions.q: Why would an admin assign a permission set instead of cloning a new profile for one user's extra need?
options: Permission sets are required by Salesforce for all users
Cloning a profile for one person's one extra need causes unnecessary profile sprawl; a permission set targets just that user
Permission sets are the only way to grant any object access at all
Profiles can no longer be cloned in modern Salesforce orgs
questions.explain: Permission sets let an admin grant a small, targeted increment of access without creating a near-duplicate profile.

questions.q: Can a permission set remove access that a user's profile already grants?
options: Yes, permission sets can both grant and revoke access
No — permission sets can only grant additional access, never take it away
Only System Administrator permission sets can revoke access
Only if the permission set is marked as restrictive
questions.explain: Permission sets are additive only, which is why assigning one is low-risk compared to changing a profile.

questions.q: How many permission sets can a single user hold at once?
options: Exactly one, same as a profile
Zero or one
Any number
A maximum of three
questions.explain: Unlike the mandatory single profile, a user can be assigned any number of permission sets.

questions.q: Where can you see every permission set that touches a specific object, and what it grants?
options: The Setup Audit Trail
The object's Object Access page in Object Manager, under the Permission Sets tab
The Translation Workbench
The Company Information page
questions.explain: Object Manager's Object Access page lists every permission set, permission set group, and profile touching that object, with their Read/Create/Edit/Delete/View All/Modify All grants.

questions.q: Where in Setup do you create a new permission set?
options: Setup > Administration > Permission Sets > New
Setup > Company Information > New
Setup > Flow > New
Setup > Email Administration > New
questions.explain: Permission Sets lives in the same Administration group as Users and Profiles, with a New button to start one.
